items.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You spoke to Patti Jones about a quote from the 19th Century English writer Walter Pater

ctx.x: I know. When she wanted to do it, Mose kept saying, “I don’t want anybody following me around, asking me a bunch of questions.” I said, “Mose!”

For part two of day one with Mose Allison, I’ll read into the record a quote at the beginning of Chapter 2 of a biography of Mose Allison called One Man’s Blues: The Life and Music of Mose Allison, by Patti Jones. It was published in 1995. Mose told her: “I left Ole Miss as a naive provincial, and when I returned I was a fledgling hipster. When I went back to Ole Miss after the army, I had become a bebop fanatic. Bebop was my crusade, Dizzy Gillespie was my hero, and I wrote arrangements for the dance band which…
